evidence.title: Paul Graham post about Apollo Atomics, Inc. / nuclear reactor startup in the YC batch
evidence.text: Paul Graham described the nuclear reactor startup in the YC batch after speaking at YC. The official YC Spring 2026 snapshot identifies Apollo Atomics, Inc. as the batch company whose tagline is "We make the most compact nuclear reactors." Native post text: When Jessica and I spoke at YC last night there was a bright flash out behind the building. We were a bit nervous because there's a nuclear reactor startup in the batch that has a bunch of hardware back there. But apparently it was just a muni cable shorting out.

evidence.title: Paul Graham post about ReasonBlocks cutting LLM token costs by about half
evidence.text: Paul Graham described doing office hours with a startup that cuts companies' LLM token costs by optimizing requests, cutting costs by about half. The official YC Spring 2026 snapshot identifies ReasonBlocks as the runtime layer that makes AI agents cheaper and cites a 52% token reduction. Native post text: Curiously enough I did office hours today with a startup that cuts companies' LLM token costs by optimizing requests. They can cut costs by about half, which they split with the customer. So the TAM is a quarter of the model companies' corporate revenue. That's a big TAM!

evidence.text:
Nebula Security is now backed by Y Combinator.

We’re celebrating by bringing you the world’s first Android 17 root demo — “IonStack”, a url click can let attacker fully control your phone.

This is not only an Android root demo. We’re bringing you a full chain browser-to-kernel exploit with two 0-day vulnerabilities affecting Firefox before v151.0.2 and all Linux distros in 15 years. "IonStack" demonstrates how bad actors can control your phone by sending a malicious URL, but good news, Nebula Security found it before attackers do.

Both 0-day were found by our code scanning agent, VEGA, overshadowing any vulnerabilities found by Mythos or any scanner you name it.

VEGA has demonstrated its extraordinary capability in finding critical bugs in the world’s most complicated software: operating systems and browsers. It can spot the same vulnerabilities in your codebase too.

VEGA support full scan and incremental scan that can integrated into your CI/CD flow. We launched VEGA within YC companies and received overwhelmingly positive feedback. Now it is open to all enterprise customers in private beta.

Book a demo with us: https://nebusec.ai/book-a-demo

evidence.text:
We raised $2.8M to bring AI hands to every Windows desktop.

Backed by: @fdotinc., Top Harvest Capital, @seedclubvc, LG Technology Ventures.

The global economy runs on legacy Windows software with no APIs. AI is exponentially smarter but can't operate in this environment because it has no hands.

Mediar gives AI its hands.

Today we're announcing we closed a $2.8M pre-seed round at a $40M valuation to turn any high-volume manual workflow into an API and automate the world economy.

We've already deployed an AI agent that:

- Watches users work
- Compiles automations autonomously
- Achieves 95% success rate and <20s latency within 1 day
- Scales across hundreds of desktops

If you've seen ChatGPT agents, Claude's Computer, or Google's Project Marin, think of Mediar as that, but 1000x faster and more reliable, designed for high-frequency, high-reliability execution.

If you want to cut costs by 90% on repetitive work without relying on brittle RPA dinosaurs, visit mediar[dot]ai.

evidence.title: We're excited to announce that Sazabi has raised an $8M seed round led by J2 Ventures, @villageglobal and @ycombinator, with participation …
evidence.text:
We're excited to announce that Sazabi has raised an $8M seed round led by J2 Ventures, @villageglobal and @ycombinator, with participation from @orangecollectv and over 60 angel investors from leading AI, developer tools, and infrastructure companies such as Vercel, Cursor, LangChain, OpenAI, Anthropic, GitHub, Replit, and Browserbase.

We plan to use the funding to expand our engineering team, accelerate product development, expand our go-to-market efforts, and deepen our integrations across modern cloud and developer platforms.

Sazabi is building observability for the AI era: a new general solution to observability that works for any workload, including agents, and uses AI to maximize speed and automation.

Our vision is self-healing software, a world where software heals and improves itself without human intervention or direction.

Join us.

🔗 Read the announcement: https://lnkd.in/ekEisGZk

evidence.text:
I got into YC S26 as a solo founder!

The last 15 months looked something like this:

> Started an API company from scratch
> Realized building infrastructure is insanely hard
> Grew slowly for months
> Then all at once
> Reached 210 paying customers
> Landed 10 unicorns + 70 VC-backed startups
> Started telling customers "not yet" because I couldn't afford to build everything they wanted
> Wait, I actually need funding
> Applied to YC
> Rejected
> Doubled revenue
> Applied again

Today I'm in.

To all my customers who trusted me when I was just some random dude from the internet, thank you.

evidence.title: Taro Fukuyama top Hardtech startups in Y Combinator P26
evidence.text:
Here's the top Hardtech startups in Y Combinator P26 by The Silicon Valley Post!
+ Adialante - Compact, mobile whole-body MRI for any clinic
+ 9 Mothers - AI-powered counter-drone systems for the U.S. government
+ General Aviation - Satellite-based ATC for every aircraft, drone, and rocket
+ Apollo Atomics (YC P26) - Pressurized water reactors small enough to ship on a flatbed
+ Dispatch | YC P26 - Reentry vehicles that bring manufactured goods back from orbit
+ Lumius (YC P26) - Affordable, portable 3D ultrasound at a fraction of the cost
+ synphony - Strawberry-picking robots and farm software for California growers
+ Eden Robotics - Semi-humanoid robots for manufacturing, rented by the hour

evidence.title: Taro Fukuyama new investment: Adialante
evidence.text:
🎉 New Investment: Adialante 🎉
I'm excited to share that I'm investing in Adialante alongside Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund.
AAdialante builds compact, mobile whole-body MRI to make cancer screening accessible to everyone. MRI is the best tool for catching cancer early, yet machines cost millions and need specialists, so patients get scanned only when it's too late. Adialante rebuilt MRI from the physics up — half the hardware, 80% lighter, whisper-quiet, full diagnostic quality. They don't sell machines; they operate them as imaging clinics on wheels, starting with prostate cancer. They already have $12.75M in LOIs and a first system scanning by demo day.
Founders Efraín Torres, PhD and Parker Jenkins are why I'm backing this. Both biomedical engineers, they met as students and spent six years inventing new MRI methods, winning millions in grants and securing patents. They pair deep technical skill with a sharp commercial wedge and the resolve to disrupt the industry.

evidence.title: Taro Fukuyama most agent-pilled startups in YC Spring 2026
evidence.text:
The 11 most "agent-pilled" startups in Y Combinator 2026 Spring batch by The Silicon Valley Post
▫️ Thomas — the first YC-backed AI founder. A virtual human that starts, runs, and grows its own companies. Not a tool for founders; the founder itself.
▫️ Humwork (YC P26) — connects stuck agents to verified human experts in under 30 seconds via MCP. Waymo's remote driver assistance, but for agents.
▫️ RentAHuman — a marketplace where AI agents hire humans for physical, regulatory, or judgment-heavy tasks.
▫️ AgentPhone — gives every agent its own phone number with voice and messaging through one API. Already used by teams at Google's ADK, Replit, Y Combinator, and LangChain.
▫️ Chronicle Labs — staging environments for enterprise agents. Captures every production event and backtests new behaviors before deployment.
▫️ InsForge — agent-native cloud infrastructure. Coding agents deploy and operate the entire backend from a single CLI.
▫️ Klaimee (YC P26) — the first purpose-built E&O coverage for AI agents, just as Berkshire, Chubb, and Travelers win approval to exclude AI liability from standard policies.
▫️ Mount — a full AI insurance carrier, starting with liability coverage for deployed agents. Two companies attacking this gap in one batch is itself a signal.
▫️ Primitive — the communication layer for agents to coordinate, hand off tasks, and share context.
▫️ Standout (YC P26) — a hiring marketplace where autonomous agents represent both candidates and companies.
▫️ Superset — the IDE for running hundreds of coding agents in parallel.

evidence.title: Taro Fukuyama new investment: Apollo Atomics
evidence.text:
🎉 New Investment: Apollo Atomics (YC P26) 🎉
I'm excited to share that I'm investing in Apollo Atomics alongside Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund.
Apollo Atomics builds compact nuclear reactors for customers who can't wait for the grid. Conventional nuclear takes over a decade and roughly $20B per plant, while most SMR startups bet on exotic fuels and supply chains that don't exist yet. Apollo keeps the pressurized water reactor technology that already powers 80% of the world's nuclear plants and redesigns just one component, the steam generator, making the plant roughly 80% smaller without compromising power. The result is a factory-built reactor that fits on a truck and deploys in under 24 months, serving data centers, industrials, and utilities. They've already built and tested a working demonstrator.
Co-founder and CEO Assil Halimi holds a PhD in Nuclear Engineering from MIT, with 18 peer-reviewed publications and two patents on reactor design. He previously worked in reactor operations at Engie and an advanced reactor designer with EDF, the world's largest nuclear operator. Co-founder and COO Drew Walker previously co-founded Blue Innovations Group, an electric boat startup, and served in the White House. Deep nuclear engineering credibility paired with commercial and operations execution. Exactly the team this industry needs.
Let's goo!

evidence.text:
The 11 most "agent-pilled" startups in Y Combinator 2026 Spring batch by The Silicon Valley Post
▫️ Thomas — the first YC-backed AI founder. A virtual human that starts, runs, and grows its own companies. Not a tool for founders; the founder itself.
▫️ Humwork (YC P26) — connects stuck agents to verified human experts in under 30 seconds via MCP. Waymo's remote driver assistance, but for agents.
▫️ RentAHuman — a marketplace where AI agents hire humans for physical, regulatory, or judgment-heavy tasks.

▫️ Chronicle Labs — staging environments for enterprise agents. Captures every production event and backtests new behaviors before deployment.
▫️ InsForge — agent-native cloud infrastructure. Coding agents deploy and operate the entire backend from a single CLI.
▫️ Klaimee (YC P26) — the first purpose-built E&O coverage for AI agents, just as Berkshire, Chubb, and Travelers win approval to exclude AI liability from standard policies.
▫️ Mount — a full AI insurance carrier, starting with liability coverage for deployed agents. Two companies attacking this gap in one batch is itself a signal.
▫️ Primitive — the communication layer for agents to coordinate, hand off tasks, and share context.
▫️ Standout (YC P26) — a hiring marketplace where autonomous agents represent both candidates and companies.
▫️ Superset — the IDE for running hundreds of coding agents in parallel.

evidence.title: Taro Fukuyama new investment: Complir
evidence.text:
🎉 New Investment: Complir 🎉
I'm excited to share that I'm investing in Complir alongside Y Combinator.
Complir is AI-native compliance infrastructure for global retailers — Vanta for physical products. Selling across markets is brutal: rules differ by country, documentation is fragmented, and regulations shift constantly, so every launch becomes a fire drill. Complir maps products to the right regulatory requirements, turns messy product data into audit-ready records, and auto-generates labels, warnings, risk assessments, and technical docs. When rules or products change, updates propagate automatically. It already manages 100,000+ products and is growing ~45% month over month.
Founders Gustav Bang, Tine Kühnel, and Marc Kaa Brejner have rare founder-market fit. Just a month after Gustav and Tine met, they landed Flying Tiger Copenhagen and embedded inside its compliance, packaging, and sourcing teams for over a year. That ground-level view showed them exactly how compliance breaks — and how to fix it.

evidence.title: Taro Fukuyama new investment: InsForge
evidence.text:
🎉 New Investment: InsForge 🎉
I'm excited to share that I'm investing in InsForge alongside Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund.
InsForge is the backend platform built for AI-native development. Backend tools today assume a human at every step, with dashboards and manual configs. As coding agents become the primary builders, that model breaks down. InsForge gives an agent one consistent CLI to deploy and operate the full backend: servers, database, auth, and storage. Every primitive returns structured outputs and readable errors, while branching, scoped permissions, and reversible writes keep changes safe to review or discard. An agent can build, run, debug, and scale an app end to end.
Hang Huang and Tony (Yaowen) Chang are a strong fit for this. Hang, the CEO, is a former Amazon product manager and former pro League of Legends player. Tony, the CTO, was a network infrastructure engineer at Databricks. Together they pair deep infrastructure depth with the conviction that coding agents will soon run entire applications on their own.

evidence.title: Taro Fukuyama new investment: Limrun
evidence.text:
🎉 New Investment: Limrun (YC P26) 🎉
I'm excited to share that I'm investing in Limrun alongside Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund.
AI coding agents now write software in the cloud, but their Linux sandboxes can't run native mobile toolchains. No Xcode, no reliable Android emulator, no clean way to build and ship iOS or Android apps. Limrun fixes this with remote Xcode, iOS Simulators, and Android Emulators that any cloud agent can call through a single skill file. An agent goes from ticket to fully tested, preview-ready pull request without ever leaving its sandbox. You can now use it with any background agent. Quizlet and Sorce are using Cursor Cloud with Limrun to build their mobile apps. Replit, Rork, and vibecode.dev already build on it, and Limrun is now opening the platform to every mobile team.
Limrun is built by Muvaffak Onuş, an emeritus maintainer of the CNCF project Crossplane and former tech lead at Upbound. He most recently led AI infrastructure work at QA Wolf, where he saw firsthand how today's sandboxes break down at scale. Few people understand cloud-native infrastructure for agents this deeply, which makes him exactly the right founder to build the mobile execution layer for the agent era.

evidence.title: Taro Fukuyama most agent-pilled startups in YC Spring 2026
evidence.text:
The 11 most "agent-pilled" startups in Y Combinator 2026 Spring batch by The Silicon Valley Post
▫️ Thomas — the first YC-backed AI founder. A virtual human that starts, runs, and grows its own companies. Not a tool for founders; the founder itself.
▫️ Humwork (YC P26) — connects stuck agents to verified human experts in under 30 seconds via MCP. Waymo's remote driver assistance, but for agents.
▫️ RentAHuman — a marketplace where AI agents hire humans for physical, regulatory, or judgment-heavy tasks.
▫️ AgentPhone — gives every agent its own phone number with voice and messaging through one API. Already used by teams at Google's ADK, Replit, Y Combinator, and LangChain.
▫️ Chronicle Labs — staging environments for enterprise agents. Captures every production event and backtests new behaviors before deployment.
▫️ InsForge — agent-native cloud infrastructure. Coding agents deploy and operate the entire backend from a single CLI.
▫️ Klaimee (YC P26) — the first purpose-built E&O coverage for AI agents, just as Berkshire, Chubb, and Travelers win approval to exclude AI liability from standard policies.
▫️ Mount — a full AI insurance carrier, starting with liability coverage for deployed agents. Two companies attacking this gap in one batch is itself a signal.
▫️ Primitive — the communication layer for agents to coordinate, hand off tasks, and share context.
▫️ Standout (YC P26) — a hiring marketplace where autonomous agents represent both candidates and companies.
▫️ Superset — the IDE for running hundreds of coding agents in parallel.

evidence.title: Taro Fukuyama new investment: Superset
evidence.text:
🎉 New Investment: Superset 🎉
I'm excited to share that I'm investing in Superset alongside Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund.
Superset is the open-source, terminal-first IDE built for the AI agents era. As developers shift from writing code line by line to orchestrating coding agents like Claude Code and Codex, the old text-editor model breaks down. Superset lets engineers run multiple agents in parallel, automate workflows, aggregate context from tickets and logs, and review changes fast.
The traction is remarkable. In just five months since launch, Superset has crossed 11K GitHub stars with 75+ contributors and become a daily driver for engineers at OpenAI, Google, and Vercel, along with major open-source projects like Homebrew and browser-use. It hit number one on Product Hunt and reached the top four on Hacker News twice, backed by a fast-growing community.
The team behind it is Avi Peltz, Kiet Ho, and Satya Patel. They are building exactly where software development is heading and have already shipped a product that the best engineers love and use every day. They move fast, listen closely to their community, and have earned deep conviction from top builders across the ecosystem. I'm thrilled to back them.

evidence.title: Taro Fukuyama most agent-pilled startups in YC Spring 2026
evidence.text:
The 11 most "agent-pilled" startups in Y Combinator 2026 Spring batch by The Silicon Valley Post
▫️ Thomas — the first YC-backed AI founder. A virtual human that starts, runs, and grows its own companies. Not a tool for founders; the founder itself.
▫️ Humwork (YC P26) — connects stuck agents to verified human experts in under 30 seconds via MCP. Waymo's remote driver assistance, but for agents.
▫️ RentAHuman — a marketplace where AI agents hire humans for physical, regulatory, or judgment-heavy tasks.
▫️ AgentPhone — gives every agent its own phone number with voice and messaging through one API. Already used by teams at Google's ADK, Replit, Y Combinator, and LangChain.
▫️ Chronicle Labs — staging environments for enterprise agents. Captures every production event and backtests new behaviors before deployment.
▫️ InsForge — agent-native cloud infrastructure. Coding agents deploy and operate the entire backend from a single CLI.
▫️ Klaimee (YC P26) — the first purpose-built E&O coverage for AI agents, just as Berkshire, Chubb, and Travelers win approval to exclude AI liability from standard policies.
▫️ Mount — a full AI insurance carrier, starting with liability coverage for deployed agents. Two companies attacking this gap in one batch is itself a signal.
▫️ Primitive — the communication layer for agents to coordinate, hand off tasks, and share context.
▫️ Standout (YC P26) — a hiring marketplace where autonomous agents represent both candidates and companies.
▫️ Superset — the IDE for running hundreds of coding agents in parallel.

evidence.text:

+ Adialante: Affordable, silent, and compact MRI systems
+ Limrun (YC P26): Cloud agent with Xcode, Android, and more
+ 9 Mothers : AI weapon systems
+ Apollo Atomics (YC P26): Rebuilding energy with revolutionary nuclear technology
+ primitive.dev (YC P26): Communication for agents
+ Superset : The IDE for the AI agents era
+ InsForge: Supabase for agents
+ General Aviation: Fixing ATC by connecting aircraft to the internet
+ Complir: Vanta for physical products
+ Dispatch: Satellites for manufacturing in space
+ Tasklet: The cloud agent operating system for knowledge work
Some of them still have room left in their rounds.
See you tomorrow!
+1
